chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Humran and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil, all together from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: concerning

A mudabbar who killed a man by mistake—he said: "If his master wishes, he should pay the diyah to them; otherwise, he hands him over to them to serve them. Then when his master dies"—meaning the one who emancipated him—he returns free. And in the narration of Yunus: "There is nothing upon him."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These narrations came in this unrestricted form, stating that whenever the mudabbir dies, the mudabbar becomes free, and there is nothing in them stating that he is to be made to work toward paying the diyah. What is more appropriate is that this be stipulated within them, so it would be said: when the master who made him mudabbar dies, he is made to work toward the diyah of the slain person, so that the blood of a Muslim man is not rendered void. That does not conflict with these reports. As for his statement in the narration of Yunus, "There is nothing upon him," we interpret it to mean that there is no punishment upon him, or that there is nothing upon him at present, even if it becomes obligatory upon him to be made to work over the passage of time. And the detail that we have mentioned was narrated by:

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money owed as financial compensation for wrongful killing
key_terms.الْعُقُوبَةِ: punishment, here distinguished from financial liability
key_terms.حُرًّا: free, no longer remaining in bondage
key_terms.خَطَأً: unintentionally or by mistake, indicating accidental killing
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master, the owner responsible for him in this ruling
key_terms.مُدَبَّرٍ: a slave promised emancipation upon the death of his master

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a mudabbar slave who commits accidental killing in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling for a mudabbar slave who kills someone by mistake, stating that the master may either pay the diyah or hand the slave over for service, and that the slave becomes free upon the master's death. Shaykh al-Tusi then explains that the reports are general in wording and argues that the slave should still be made to work toward the diyah after emancipation so that the blood of a Muslim is not left uncompensated.
